original_record.subject: accounts
original_record.question: In a public corporation, the capital expenditure incurred in a financial period is

options.A: spread over the useful life of the assets through depreciation
options.B: apportioned at a pre-determined rate stipulated by law
options.C: written off in the year in which they occur
options.D: merged with recurrent expenditure and reported in one lump sum.

original_record.ai_explanation: Capital expenditure in public corporations is spread over the useful life of assets through depreciation rather than written off immediately.

records.hold_reason: Capital expenditure can include non-depreciable assets such as land. The source generalises depreciation over all capital expenditure without specifying a depreciable asset or framework.

original_record.ai_explanation: Under cash accounting, money not required to meet chargeable expenditure in a fiscal year must be surrendered to the consolidated revenue fund.
